subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Second-Life Batteries
description: A fast breakdown of Second-Life Batteries for builders.

hook.text: When an EV battery drops below 80 percent capacity, it's no longer great for driving—but far from dead.

buildup.text: These retired packs still hold huge amounts of energy, perfect for less demanding applications.

discovery.text: Old EV batteries are being repurposed as stationary storage for solar panels and grid backup.

twist.text: Nissan and BMW already run projects where retired car batteries power buildings and stabilize grids.

climax.text: Second-life use could extend the total value of each battery by a decade before recycling is needed.

punchline.text: An EV battery's second career might last longer than its first.

quiz.question: What happens to EV batteries when they drop below 80% capacity?
options: They can be reused for stationary energy storage
